title: Latency-tiered token econ playbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick playbook + scratch spreadsheet for exploring a latency-tiered pricing approach for Hosted API. Focus: per-token COGS by model+region, margin floors by latency tier (p50/p95/p99), and the interaction with quantization/batching levers. This is an exploratory working sheet — lots of rough numbers + explicit assumptions.

High-level hypothesis:
- Customers value predictable latency slices (e.g., interactive vs background) and are willing to pay a premium for tighter p95/p99 latency SLOs. If we price by latency tier and surface quantization/batch levers, we can:
  1) increase realized ASP for interactive traffic,
  2) reduce costs on background/cheaper tiers via aggressive quantization and batching,
  3) preserve margins by attaching margin floors to latency tiers rather than raw model family.

Key assumptions (work in progress):
- GPU cost basis (amortized incl infra & ops) by region (USD/hour): US-EAST: 3.60, EU-WEST: 4.10, APAC-SG: 4.70. (source: infra run-rate Nov 2025)
- Token throughput per GPU varies by model & quantization. Example steady-state throughput (tokens/sec/GPU):
  - redwood-13b-fp16: 220
  - redwood-13b-8bit: 480
  - openchat-7b-4bit: 730
  - mpt-30b-8bit: 160
- Effective utilization factor (avg across tenant mix after batching): interactive tier 0.55, background tier 0.80.
- Average response sequence length (generated tokens) by workload: interactive 60 tokens, background 600 tokens.

Quick per-token cost formula (used in table below):
  per_token_cogs = (gpu_hour_cost / (throughput_tokens_per_sec * 3600 * utilization)) + infra_fixed_per_token_overlay
  - infra_fixed_per_token_overlay (network, storage, orchestration) = $0.0000009 (placeholder)

=== Snapshot: illustrative per-token COGS by model & region ===
(note: round numbers, don't treat as finalized)
CSV_HEADER: model,quant,region,throughput_tps,use_util,base_gpu_hr_cost,per_token_cogs_usd
redwood-13b,fp16,us-east,220,0.55,3.60,0.0000101
redwood-13b,8bit,us-east,480,0.55,3.60,0.0000048
openchat-7b,4bit,eu-west,730,0.55,4.10,0.0000029
mpt-30b,8bit,apac,160,0.55,4.70,0.0000166
redwood-13b,8bit,apac,480,0.80,4.70,0.0000024

Observations from snapshot:
- Quantization (8-bit/4-bit) drives 2–4x per-token COGS improvement on the same model family.
- Utilization matters more than nominal throughput: background workloads with higher utilization can have significantly lower effective per-token cost.
- APAC has a material delta vs US-EAST in base GPU hour — we need regional pricing adjustments to retain margin parity.

Margin framing and pricing tiers (initial sketches):
- Define three latency tiers per route: interactive (p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms), standard (p50 < 500ms, p95 < 1.2s), background (no tight p95; best-effort).
- Attach a margin floor to each tier (net of per-token COGS): interactive 45% margin floor, standard 30%, background 18%. Margin floor is target net margin after infra/ops overhead and expected discounts.
- Pricing examples (list price per 1k tokens):
  - redwood-13b fp16 US-EAST: interactive $0.078 / 1k tokens, standard $0.054 / 1k, background $0.028 / 1k
  - redwood-13b 8bit US-EAST: interactive $0.045 / 1k, standard $0.032 / 1k, background $0.016 / 1k
  - openchat-7b 4bit EU-WEST: interactive $0.028 / 1k, standard $0.019 / 1k, background $0.010 / 1k
(These anchor prices are rough and based on per_token_cogs * (1 / (1 - margin_floor))).

Short spreadsheet fragment: per-token delta sensitivity (how price changes per 10% utilization shift)
CSV_HEADER: model,region,quant,base_util,util_minus10pct,per_token_base,per_token_minus10pct,delta_pct
redwood-13b,us-east,8bit,0.55,0.495,0.0000048,0.0000053,11.0%
openchat-7b,eu-west,4bit,0.55,0.495,0.0000029,0.0000032,10.3%

Recommendations & actionable experiments (short list):
1) Pilot tiered pricing on a select set of routes (2–3 customers) where we can control routing policy. Offer bundle: interactive-tier SLA + auto-fallback to standard if capacity constrained; bill at interactive rate while SLA met. Measure revenue uplift and SLA compliance.
2) Expose a customer-facing dashboard that shows effective per-token cost drivers (quantization, avg batch size, p95 latency) per route. This will increase willingness to adopt lower-cost tiers.
3) Run 2-week infra experiments to push batch size heuristics for 'background' traffic and instrument seq length distributions more precisely. Estimate delta on per-token COGS and update region price decks.
4) For APAC, refactor reserved pool placement and price multipliers; evaluate whether dedicated capacity discounts are needed to keep margin parity.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Do we want to make latency tiers first-class in the API (route-level SLA flags) or start as an opt-in pricing SKU? Pros/cons listed in comments.
- How to account for cold-start KV-cache warmups in per-token calc? Early drafts exclude warmup overhead; this likely underestimates interactive costs by ~5–12% depending on request shape.
- Should we offer an explicit quantization discount program (e.g., 15% off interactive tier for 8-bit models) or bake it into base prices?

Notes to reviewers (rough):
- This is intentionally heuristic — most of the numbers are placeholders we can quickly replace with infra run-rate exports (Infra Cost center) and production p95 telemetry.
- Next update will add a per-customer profitability slice and a small Monte Carlo for seq-length variance.

Quick TODOs (owner initials):
